original.target_description: Study 2: London undergraduates; BCTI post-manipulation analytic scrambled-sentence prime versus control, independent-samples t-test.

n.quote: The participants of this study were 112 undergraduates
n.sample_role: participants in the target between-condition test
n.exclusions: Six unreachable participants omitted before the final 112; 68 pilot participants excluded from main-study participation.

replication.target_description: Replication Study 1: UK Prolific participants; BCTI post-test analytic scrambled-sentence prime versus control, independent-samples t-test.

n.quote: After removing responses that did not pass preregistered quality checks (see below) in one of the two waves (n = 14), we were left with N = 302 participants (147 in the experimental and 155 in the control condition).
n.sample_role: participants in the target between-condition test
n.exclusions: 316 completed both waves; 14 removed by preregistered quality checks. Main analysis before optional outlier/hypothesis-guessing exclusions.

reported_success.quote: Overall, we found no evidence that the analytical prime group decreased in belief in conspiracy theories.

notes: Titles verified against supplied references in both full-text PDFs. Original locator p. 7 uses PDF pagination; replication locator p. 4 uses printed pagination. Main post-test between-condition comparison selected because it prints requested d; not the interaction or within-analytic paired test. A general web search incidentally surfaced forbidden-site snippets; those were not opened or used as extraction evidence.
